kind: independent finite synchronous FileHandle close C helper and retained native lifetime source peer

findings.subject: Actual synchronous operation
findings.result: The added helper asserts non-null service/request and calls the original uv_fs_close(&service->loop, request, descriptor, NULL). It returns the actual native integer status without allocating PiUvFsRequest, submitting a service command, changing request waiting counters, or adding a callback.
findings.authority: Projected native_uv_tcp.c finite 461-byte insertion; projected header finite signature and caller-owned request contract.

findings.subject: Windows null-callback path
findings.result: INIT calls the original uv__fs_req_init. That function performs the existing global once initialization and initializes the request; its loop use is the request loop-pointer store. UV_REQ_INIT sets request type and overlapped status. POST selects uv__fs_work directly when cb is NULL, bypassing loop registration and work submission. Selected CLOSE dispatch reaches fs__close and returns request.result.

findings.subject: Windows actual descriptor close and cleanup
findings.result: fs__close retains the original descriptor validation, synchronized fd-hash removal, file-map CloseHandle handling, and _close/result translation. The fd hash uses its original global uv_mutex. The selected close and uv_fs_req_cleanup operate on descriptor/global/request state and do not dereference the supplied loop.

findings.subject: Unix null-callback path
findings.result: INIT stores the loop pointer in the request. The callback-gated io_uring branch is skipped for NULL; POST calls uv__fs_work directly and returns its result. CLOSE calls uv__fs_close, which invokes uv__close_nocancel on the integer descriptor and preserves the original EINTR/EINPROGRESS handling. The selected worker path does not retry CLOSE for EINTR. Cleanup uses request-owned fields, with no loop dereference.

findings.subject: Canonical caller-owned native request
findings.result: The GC caller declares native_uv.uv_fs_t on its stack. native_uv comes through StreamResource to the actual managed-buffers @cImport of uv.h, whose typedef and struct are the original uv_fs_s layout. The narrow C declaration accepts struct uv_fs_s*. There is no guessed byte-storage extent or hand-written struct layout.

findings.subject: Original caller sequencing
findings.result: The selected GC source checks closed/closing and fd, then performs trace BEGIN, synchronous close, trace END and uv_fs_req_cleanup before capturing the descriptor and running AfterClose. Its result is captured at the call. The queued Ticket later contains result/descriptor scalars and an independently retained Environment; it does not retain the stack request, FileHandle pointer or service loop pointer. Refed selection result < 0 matches the original error versus successful warning branches.
findings.authority: node_file.cc 336-391; selected complete gc_close source and explicit ordered anchors in source-audit.json.

findings.subject: Retained service storage across close and stop
findings.result: Handle.create retains the Controller before native initialization. Handle.retire invokes GC close before member and StreamBase teardown and before releaseInfrastructure releases the Controller. Controller publication retains PiUvService; its final release drops that entitlement, while Hub stopped drops only the Hub Controller reference. PiUvService embeds uv_loop_t and frees its allocation only on the final service reference. Thus the reviewed caller retains the loop member address/storage through the complete synchronous call, trace END and cleanup, including the selected already-joined service state. The helper does not require ordinary asynchronous Controller admission for this direct operation.
findings.authority: owner.zig 96-143 and 178-220; projected fs_request_io.zig 20-41, 199-229, 300-320; projected native_uv_tcp.c 127-152, 169-183, 652-657, 711-723.

scope_limits: This peer does not qualify the complete FileHandle owner, CloseReq Promise policy, ordinary JavaScript continuation, warning/exception delivery or the entire shared five-file proposal. Handover is reviewing that broader unit independently.
The trace callbacks and actual native queue/bootstrap owners remain explicit assembly dependencies. This peer supplies no no-op trace or queue implementation.

The source mapping demonstrates the selected null-callback branches and retained native storage. No compiler-selected ABI, native execution, concurrent descriptor behavior, platform qualification or whole-application behavior was observed.
The original frozen 061258BF/C195 proposals remain unchanged. Later additive CloseReq corrections are outside this helper peer.
